newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - April 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - April 2.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Pakistani parliament on Tuesday stripped the president and the governors of their powers to dissolve the assemblies with the unanimous annulment of the controversial sections of the Eighth Amendment in the constitution.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has said the repeal of the controversial parts of the Eighth Amendment would lead to political consensus on major issues and bring about economic stability.
- Opposition leader Benazir Bhutto has termed the scrapping of the controversial parts a major victory for all workers and leaders who had made sacrifices for parliamentary democracy.
- The government borrowed $1.53 billion in foreign exchange and 76.3 billion rupees from domestic sources during July 1996 to February 1997.
- The government is considering a major reduction in the number of government ministries and divisions besides downsizing public sector corporations.
- Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan has said a proposed meeting with his Indian counterpart might be postponed in the wake of the political crisis in India.

- The government is launching a hydel power policy by initially offering 12 small and medium sized hydel power generation projects of 3,610 megawatt capacity, requiring an investment of $4,280 million.
- BHP Petroleum of Australia has submitted a proposal to the government for an off-shore gas pipeline between Iran and Pakistan.
- Pakistani traders and industrialists have been invited to take part in the second Bangladesh business roundtable beginning in Dhaka from May 22 to 27.
- Ukraine is to deliver a second batch of 35 T-80 UD tanks to Pakistan as part of its deal to provide 300 tanks. It delivered first batch of 15 tanks last month.

- The prime minister's adviser on law and justice, Anwar Khalid, said on Tuesday that the Council for National Defence and Security, a watchdog body set up by the former caretaker government, can be disbanded any time.
